deities: Sri Anjaneya Swamy (Lord Hanuman - idol installed facing east)

history.dynasty: Vijayanagara Empire (16th century tradition); Gadwal kings
history.period: Idol tradition 15th-16th century; mandapa ~200 years ago
history.summary: The Beechupalli Anjaneya Swamy Temple is a famous Hanuman shrine on the banks of the Krishna river in Itikyal mandal, Jogulamba Gadwal district. Tradition holds the Hanuman idol was installed by Sri Vyasa Raya (Vyasaraja, royal priest/guru of Krishnadevaraya and great Dvaita philosopher, 1457-1539); the village name derives from Beechupalli, a young tribal devotee who was the first to worship the installed idol. Around 200 years ago the Gadwal kings built a spacious mandapa over the sanctum facing south, with the Hanuman idol facing east; a Shiva lingam temple stands near the river and a Sri Rama temple was added in 1992. The region around the Krishna and Tungabhadra had great historical importance under the Mauryas, Satavahanas, Ikshvakus, Badami Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, Kalyani Chalukyas, Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara kings (per temple inscriptions). The site is sacred for Pushkara snanam (ghats built for the 12-year Krishna Pushkaralu) and for obsequies to the departed. name: Beechupalli Anjaneya Swamy Temple
town_description: Beechupally is a village in Itikyal mandal, Jogulamba Gadwal district, Telangana, on the banks of the Krishna river ~30 km downstream of the Jurala Project, on NH44 (Hyderabad-Bengaluru), ~15 km from Gadwal. Two river islands lie nearby - Gurram Gadda (larger) and Nizam Konda (smaller).

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~180 km).
travel.railway: Gadwal is the nearest railway station (~15 km).
travel.road: On NH44 (Hyderabad-Bengaluru), ~220 km from Hyderabad and ~15 km from Gadwal; 200 yards off the highway.

visitor_information.best_time: Hanuman Jayanthi in April; monsoon when the river flows high is scenic; Krishna Pushkaram year.
